tens_order.source: Store norske leksikon, "den nye tellemåten": "gjorde Stortinget enstemmig vedtak 22. november 1950 om å innføre den nye tellemåten"; "Den nye tellemåten ble innført fra 1. juli 1951."; "Uttalen av 23 ble for eksempel endret fra tre og tjue / tre og tyve til tjuetre." Store norske leksikon, "den gamle tellemåten": "I den gamle tellemåten settes enerleddet først, deretter og, og så tierleddet:" "21: én og tjue / én og tyve"; "Den gamle tellemåten brukes fortsatt i dagligtale, særlig blant eldre og i konservative talemålsformer." So both orders are read, and the old order is written as separate words.

ten_joins_unit_ordinal.source: The ordinal 13th is one word, "trettande", so "ten" and a unit ordinal are two numbers: Nynorsk ordinals end in -ande: Nynorskordboka, "tiande" (article 78684): "rekkjetal til ti (10.)"; "tjuande" (article 79531): "rekkjetal til 20". CLDR has no nn ordinal rules; the other words follow the same pattern (not checked against the page)

ordinal_joiner_by_place.source: An ordinal takes the joiner that the cardinal word in its place takes. Between a ten and a unit (never): The new order puts the unit after the ten with no joiner: CLDR RBNF nn (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, nn.xml), %spellout-cardinal-reale: "20: tjue[→→]"; CLDR RBNF nn (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, nn.xml), %spellout-cardinal-reale: 21 → "tjueéin" After a hundred (optional): CLDR RBNF nn (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, nn.xml), %spellout-cardinal-reale: "100: ←%spellout-cardinal-neuter← hundre[ og →→]"

joiner_before_last_group.source: CLDR RBNF nn (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, nn.xml), %spellout-cardinal-reale: "1000: ←%spellout-cardinal-neuter← tusen[ og →→]" writes "og" before the last group. No source read says that a last group with no "og" starts a new number, so the reader takes both forms.

one_before_ordinal_scale_is_fraction.source: A fraction is the ordinal and "-del" ("hundredel"), so a count of one before an ordinal scale word makes an ordinal: CLDR RBNF nb (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, no.xml), %spellout-ordinal-masculine: 100 → "énhundrede", 1000 → "éntusende"

period_ordinals.source: An ordinal in digits takes a period, as "17. mai" (Språkrådet, "Tal"; rule quoted from memory, the page refused automated reading). A period also ends a sentence, so only a lower-case word after it, as month names are (CLDR month names for Norwegian Nynorsk (Babel 2.18.0): "januar", "februar", "mars", "april", "mai", "juni", "juli", "august", "september", "oktober", "november", "desember"), or "den" before the digits makes it an ordinal mark: "i 1905. Dette" is the cardinal 1905.
